name: recipes
description: A recipe box: recipes read from a folder of text files, scaling to a number of servings, unit conversion and a merged shopping list.
author: harness developer (dev split)

issues.description: scaled_amount takes (amount, servings, wanted) but scale passes wanted and the recipe's servings the other way round, so doubling a recipe halves every amount.
The docstring says ingredient names match ignoring case, but the merge key only strips spaces, so "Flour" and "flour" end up on two lines.
issues.fix_hint: Lower-case the name in the merge key as well as stripping it.

issues.description: The docstring says converting between mass, volume and pieces raises ValueError, but the dimensions are thrown away and never compared, so 100 g silently becomes 100 ml.
issues.fix_hint: Keep both dimensions and raise ValueError when they differ.

issues.description: Quantities from recipe files are run with eval, so a shared .recipe file can execute any Python code when the folder is loaded.
issues.fix_hint: Parse numbers and a/b fractions explicitly (float, Fraction) and raise ValueError for anything else.

issues.description: The shopping list reads recipes from a module-level dict that the file loader fills, so the domain logic depends on the I/O module and on hidden global state: it only works after load_folder ran, and callers cannot pass their own recipes.
The private helper _fraction_text is never called anywhere; it (and the Fraction import it needs) is dead code.
A nine-branch if/elif ladder maps spellings to units; the aliases are data and belong in a lookup table next to UNITS.

decoys.why_it_is_fine: The broad except only logs which file failed and re-raises the original error, so nothing is swallowed.
The tiny tolerance stops float noise from scaling (3.0000000000000004 eggs) from rounding up to an extra piece; real fractions such as 2.1 still round up.
